page_title: Tokenized Money Market Funds — Digital Assets Dashboard
page_subtitle_html: Tokenized money market fund (MMF) exposure aggregated from RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt. Networks and platforms are built from each fund's on-chain token deployments; Distributed Value columns are current levels.
kpi_window_note: Distributed value uses a 30-day (30D) % change vs summed token values 30 days ago. Top network share is the largest network by distributed value; the 30D figure is the change in market-share percentage points (pp), not a percent of total. Fund universe: fixed curated TMMF population on RWA.xyz US Treasuries and Non-U.S. Government Debt; KPIs, charts, and league tables use the same fund set.
key_observations_html:
Key observations

  • TMMF distributed value fell 3.8% over 30D: With distributed value at $12.66B (3.8% lower over 30D). Related: HSBC Opens Tokenized Fund Subscriptions With RedCoin (The Defiant).
  • Early "flight to efficiency" shows up in TMMF 30D network share: Among tokenized money market funds, gainers include Stellar (+8.60% 30D TMMF network share), Solana (+0.76% 30D TMMF network share); losers include Ethereum (-7.59% 30D TMMF network share), Avalanche C-Chain (-1.09% 30D TMMF network share). That pattern is consistent with TMMF issuers routing more distributed value toward higher-throughput, lower-fee chains—though Ethereum still dominates TMMF share levels in most snapshots. Related: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement between tokenized deposits and money market funds (The Block).
  • Multi-chain footprints are a distribution signal: Funds listing many networks with thin holder counts usually signal jurisdictional or distribution reach, not deep secondary liquidity on every chain. Related: Trump's Democratic SEC pick suggests tokenization policy deserves full rule process (CoinDesk).
  • Regulatory framing still decides product access: Similar funds can sit under different investor-eligibility and jurisdiction labels, so compliance framing still decides who can hold and distribute them. Related: Who Decides Which Chains Count as Public? | Cosmos, Zenith, Injective (The Defiant).
  • Issuer strategies are splitting into two models: Institutional cash rail programs (low holder counts, large AUM per holder—e.g. USYC, iBENJI, BUIDL, JLTXX) vs global yield / distribution products (broader holder bases, retail- or UCITS-friendly framing—e.g. USDY, BENJI, WTGXX, USTBL). These behave like different businesses under the same "tokenized MMF" label. Related: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading (CoinTelegraph).

Context only—not investment advice. Observations rank fund-level and network aggregates on this page against recent tokenization and money-market headlines. Bullets combine on-page data with recent industry headlines.

Key observations are AI generated and should be reviewed for accuracy.
